# PREFACE
->BY<-
# JOHANNES WESSELIUS
->To the READER, who pursues truth in love.<-

->*Dealing with the ETERNAL TESTAMENT*<-
->*of Grace, and the ETERNAL COVENANT between*<-
->*the FATHER and the SON.*<-

More than one work, out of a very large number of others published in Latin and French by the highly learned and exceptionally industrious Lord B. PICTET <note>Benedict Pictet (1655–1724) was a prominent Swiss Reformed theologian from Geneva whose works were highly influential in the Netherlands.</note>, now sees the light in our Dutch language. To his excellent **CHRISTIAN ETHICS**, translated and published in the year 1720, this large and outstanding work, the **CHRISTIAN THEOLOGY**, which is now offered to you, is a very fitting addition; because from both of these, one can learn everything required for the practice of true <term>Godliness: translated from "Godt-saligheid," referring to a life of active piety and devotion to God.</term>, as well as for the knowledge of the Truth that leads to godliness. The first Volume now definitely leads the way, while the Other shall follow quickly. The translation has been carried out by a capable hand, which is master of both languages and fully knowledgeable of the subject matter. These two qualities are necessary in a good translator. The work itself shows throughout marks of its fine author, and one can see that it has proceeded from the hand and pen of an orthodox, thoroughly learned, prudent, and modest theologian. Although one finds many glorious and perfect treatises on our Christian Theology, even in our own language, one will nevertheless encounter something in this work by Lord PICTET that is either not discussed elsewhere, or certainly not in that manner, nor so extensively. Old and new disputes are here recalled and settled. Our doctrine is compared with that of the Early Fathers <note>The "Early Fathers" or "Church Fathers" refers to the influential Christian theologians of the first few centuries AD.</note>, and to this end, their own words from their writings are faithfully cited. Lord PICTET writes everywhere about Divine matters in a learned style, and with a deep reverence for the high and unsearchable nature of the mysteries of our faith. He wishes to subject no one blindly to his authority, as befits a modest theologian. He reasons acutely, and with lively emotions for the truth, but also from firm foundations laid in the Holy Book. He refutes powerfully, but also at the same time gently, in order to convince and improve opponents, not to embitter them. Here and there, from contemporary writings of overseas authors, he reveals hidden reefs and dangerous sandbanks <note>A common maritime metaphor in Dutch literature of this period, warning readers that certain foreign theological ideas could lead to spiritual "shipwreck" or heresy.</note>, upon which the inexperienced—and those who daily read these writings translated into our language—could suffer a deadly shipwreck. He furthermore expresses himself very naturally, and is at the same time dignified and smooth-flowing in his writing style. Finally, Lord PICTET follows

# PREFACE

in this work, following in the footsteps of those Old Heroes <note>Wesselius refers here to the "Old Heroes" of the Reformation, such as John Calvin and Theodore Beza.</note> who formerly secured Zion’s foundations in the so-famous Church and School of GENEVA. For this reason, one must never blame these brave theologians if people should ever happen to deviate from that so-highly praised Mother Church and School of Old Orthodoxy; to loosen the necessary bonds of unity; or to introduce a soul-destroying indifference in Religion. May God graciously forbid such a thing, or thwart and smother it in its beginnings!

I have until now in my Academic Exercises, dealing with Holy Theology, followed the guide of the *Christian Theology*, published in Latin by Lord PICTET in the year 1696 in octavo <note>A book size where the sheet is folded three times to form eight leaves.</note>, being a short summary of this current large work, which he afterwards published in French. And this is possibly the reason why I have been requested, should I have any further observations on this or that matter treated herein, to share the same with the public on this occasion. I have finally granted this request, because I found no great reason to refuse it.

Lord PICTET, dealing with the <term>DECREE OF ELECTION: translated from "Besluit der Verkiesinge," the Calvinist doctrine that God has eternally chosen certain individuals for salvation.</term>, does indeed bring forward some expressions used in Holy Scripture to indicate it. However, he does not include among them the Hebrew word <gloss>Berith</gloss> <note>original: ברית</note> or the Greek <gloss>Diatheekee</gloss> <note>original: διαθήκη</note>, which means TESTAMENT and COVENANT. It has, however, become very common today—after several great men had led the way—that one calls this Eternal purpose of grace in Christ a TESTAMENT, and indeed an ETERNAL TESTAMENT: as well as that one views and presents the same as a COVENANT made from eternity between the Father and the Son.

Regarding the *first* name, TESTAMENT, it is argued that Paul leads the way so explicitly, giving that name to the Decree of Election in *Hebrews 13:20*, where he mentions the *blood of the* ETERNAL TESTAMENT, *that is, that which was made from eternity.* In such a sense, the word *eternal* being taken here, it can be nothing other than God’s eternal gracious purpose; which is also for that reason called a *Book of Life*, in which the names of the future heirs of blessedness are written *before the foundation of the world. Revelation 13:8; 17:8.*

One also brings forward here another passage from Paul in the *Epistle to the Galatians, Chapter 3:17*, where he speaks of a <gloss>Diatheekee</gloss>, that is, as it is translated, a TESTAMENT, *that was confirmed before by God*, <gloss>eis Christon</gloss> <note>original: εἰς χριστὸν</note>, which is to say, not *upon Christ*, but *unto Christ*, as it is noted that the preposition <gloss>eis</gloss> <note>original: εἰς</note> is taken in this way in *Ephesians 1:5* and *Colossians 1:20.* This *Testament* is subsequently held to be God's Eternal Counsel and Decree to bless and justify the Heathen in communion with Abraham's seed through faith. Which eternal Decree was confirmed, specifically through the Promise (here clearly distinguished from the *Testament* if one wishes), *spoken to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ, to whom it was promised, verses 16, 19*, namely in those words, *in you, and, in your seed, shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, verse 8*, compared with *Genesis 12:3; 18:18; 22:18.*

One appeals further to the words of our Savior in *Luke 22:29.*

<meta>This page continues the discussion on theological terminology, specifically addressing why some theologians use the terms "Testament" and "Covenant" to describe God's eternal decree of election, a point Wesselius noted was missing from Pictet's summary on the previous page.</meta>

BY JOHANNES WESSELIUS

<margin>Also Cocceius, *Summary*, Chapter XL, § 18.</margin>
And I ordain, <gloss>I bequeath; original: "diatithemai"</gloss> make by TESTAMENT to you the Kingdom, just as my Father has ordained, <gloss>bequeathed; original: "dietheto"</gloss> made by TESTAMENT to me <note>Luke 22:29</note>, namely, in himself, and by himself, in his Eternal Purpose. For, it is said, the Greek *diatithesthai* signifies, first, the internal act of the mind and the will. And it is primarily from this passage that one speaks of an Eternal Testament of the Father, to make the Son Heir of all things: and of an Eternal Testament of the Son, to make those who have been given to him by the Father—through the gift of Faith in him—heirs of righteousness, of the world, and of the Heavenly Kingdom, and so co-heirs with Him, who is the Heir of all things. Indeed, it sometimes seems that one wishes to say that the Hebrew word *Berith* <note>original: ברית</note>, which commonly signifies a Covenant, and which the Greek Translators of the Old Testament translate as *diatheke* <note>original: διαθήκη</note>, might also sometimes be taken for God’s internal and unchangeable Purpose. To which end one cites, among others, Jeremiah 33:20-21: "Thus says the LORD; if you could nullify my Covenant <note>original: "Berithi"</note>, or rather, my unchangeable Purpose and unalterable Appointment, of the day, and my Covenant, or rather Purpose and Decree, of the night, so that day and night would not be in their time." From which one concludes that it is no wonder that the word *Diatheke* is used in the New Testament for *Berith* when it refers to the "eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Ephesians 3:11).

Furthermore, it is noted that since Eternal Election is a pre-ordination to adoption as children (Ephesians 1:5), and thus to being heirs according to Romans 8:17—"And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ"—it must naturally follow that one should hold that very election to be a TESTAMENT, which is a disposition of inheritance <term>Erfschikkinge: a legal arrangement or "settlement" of an inheritance</term>, also according to Divine Revelation.

Finally, it is shown how clearly and powerfully this name of TESTAMENT, given to the Eternal Decree of election, indicates its true nature, and how many glorious and necessary truths are thereby further confirmed. Thus, this name would indicate the unchangeableness of God’s Counsel (Hebrews 6:17), because a Testament is a Last Will, and as such is fixed and not changed. Thus it would also have to follow that the Decree of Election concerns specific persons, whose names are therefore said to be written in the Book of Life, as noted above; and who are therefore called <gloss>the called; original: "kekleemenoi"</gloss> in this Testament (Hebrews 9:15), with regard to a human testament, in which the heirs are usually expressed by name. Thus also, finally, by this name it would be indicated that the execution of the Purpose of Grace depended on the Surety-death <term>Borgdoot: the death of Christ as the 'Surety' or legal guarantor who fulfills the conditions of the covenant on behalf of others</term> of the Testament-maker (Hebrews 9:15–18); which in a special way is the Son, according to Luke 22:29: "I make by Testament to you the Kingdom."

One cannot deny that this view is presented and urged with the appearance of truth and usefulness; and one must by no means doubt that it is taught with a good intention by many prominent theologians. It is however also true, that no less famous and great men

<meta>This page transitions from defending the orthodoxy of the Genevan school to a technical discussion on whether God's eternal decree of salvation should be called a "Covenant" or "Testament," terms Wesselius notes were omitted in Pictet's original summary. ->P R E F A C E<-

...in this work, following the path of those Old Heroes who once secured the foundations of Zion in the famous Church and School of GENEVA. For this reason, these brave theologians <note>literally "God-learned ones"</note> should never be blamed if one were ever to depart from that highly praised Mother Church and School of Ancient Orthodoxy; to loosen the necessary bonds of unity, and to introduce a soul-destroying indifference in religion. May God graciously forbid this, or halt and smother it in its beginnings!

Until now, in my Academic Exercises concerning Holy Theology, I have followed the guide of *Christian Theology*, published in Latin by Mr. PICTET in the year 1696 in octavo. This was a short summary of this present great work, which he afterwards published in French. This is possibly the reason why I have been requested—should I have any further remarks on this or that subject treated herein—to share them with the public on this occasion. I finally granted this request, because I found no great reason to refuse it.

Mr. PICTET, when dealing with the <term>DECREE OF ELECTION</term> <note>the theological concept that God chooses certain individuals for salvation before the world began</note>, does bring forward some expressions used in Holy Scripture to indicate it. However, among these, he does not include the Hebrew word <term>Berith</term> <note>original: ברית; meaning "Covenant"</note>, or the Greek <term>Diatheke</term> <note>original: Διαθηκη; meaning "Testament" or "Covenant"</note>, that is, TESTAMENT and COVENANT. It has, however, become very common today—following the lead of several great men—to call this Eternal Purpose of grace in Christ a TESTAMENT, and specifically an ETERNAL TESTAMENT; as well as to consider and present it as a COVENANT made between the Father and the Son from eternity.

Regarding the first name, TESTAMENT, it is argued that Paul clearly leads the way and gives this name to the Decree of Election in *Hebrews 13:20*, where he speaks of *the blood of the ETERNAL TESTAMENT*, that is, one made from *eternity*. If the word *eternal* is taken in such a sense here, it can be nothing other than God's eternal decree of grace; which is also for that reason called a *Book of Life*, in which the names of the future heirs of salvation are written *before the foundation of the world. Revelation 13:8; 17:8.*

<margin>Heidegger, *Body of Theology*, Book V. § XXVI.</margin>
<margin>Cocceius, *On the Covenant*, Chapter V. § 8.</margin>
Another passage from Paul is also brought forward here from the *Epistle to the Galatians, Chapter 3:17*, where he speaks of a <term>Diatheke</term> <note>original: Διαθηκη</note>, that is, if translated, a TESTAMENT, *which was confirmed before by God*, <term>eis Christon</term> <note>original: εις χριστον; "to Christ"</note>, that is, not "upon" Christ, but "to" Christ, as it is noted that the preposition <term>eis</term> <note>original: εις</note> is used this way in *Ephesians 1:5* and *Colossians 1:20*. This *Testament* is subsequently understood to be God’s Eternal Counsel and Decree to bless and justify the Gentiles in communion with Abraham's seed through faith. This eternal Decree of God is confirmed, especially by the Promise (which some wish to distinguish clearly from the Testament here), spoken to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ, to whom it was promised, *verses 16, 19*, namely in those words: *in you, and, in your seed, shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, verse 8*, compared with *Genesis 12:3; 18:18; 22:18.*

One further appeals to the words of our Savior in *Luke 22:29.*

# BY JOHANNES WESSELIUS

"And I ordain, <gloss>diatithemai</gloss> <note>original: διατιθεμαι; meaning "I appoint" or "I bequeath"</note>, I make by TESTAMENT to you the Kingdom, just as my Father has ordained (it) to me, <gloss>dietheto</gloss> <note>original: διέθετο; the past tense of the same verb</note>, has made by TESTAMENT," namely, in himself, and by himself, in His Eternal Purpose. For, it is said, the Greek <term>diatithesthai</term> <note>original: διατιθεσθαι; to arrange, dispose, or make a will</note> signifies, first, the internal act of the mind and the will. 
<margin>See Cocceius, *Summa*, Chapter XL, Section 18.</margin>
And it is primarily from this passage <note>Luke 22:29</note> that one speaks of an *Eternal Testament of the Father*, to make the Son the Heir of all things; and of an *Eternal Testament of the Son*, to make those who are given to Him by the Father—through the gift of Faith in Him—into Heirs of righteousness, of the world, and of the Heavenly Kingdom, and so to make them co-heirs with Him, who is the Heir of all things. Indeed, it sometimes seems one wishes to say that the Hebrew word *Berith* <note>original: ברית</note>, which commonly signifies a *Covenant*, and which the Greek Translators of the Old Testament translate as *diatheke*, might also sometimes be taken for God’s *internal and unchangeable Purpose*. To which end one brings forward, among others, *Jeremiah 33:20–21*:
> Thus says the LORD: If you people could nullify My *Berithi* [My Covenant], or rather, My unchangeable Purpose and unalterable Determination, of the day, and My Covenant, or rather Purpose and Decree, of the night, so that day and night would not be at their appointed time.
From which it is concluded that it is no wonder if, in the New Testament, the word *Diatheke* <note>original: Διαθηκη; meaning both Covenant and Testament</note> is used for *Berith* when the "Purpose of the Ages," which God has made in Christ Jesus our Lord (*Ephesians 3:11*), is intended.

Furthermore, it is noted that, as *Eternal Election* is a *pre-ordination to adoption as Children* (*Ephesians 1:5*), and thus to *Heirs according to Romans 8:17*—"And if we are Children, then we are also Heirs: Heirs of God, and co-heirs of Christ"—it must follow of itself that one must also hold that same Election as a TESTAMENT, which is an *Inheritance-arrangement*, according to Divine Revelation.

Finally, it is shown how clearly and powerfully this name of TESTAMENT, given to the Eternal Decree of election, indicates its true nature, and how many glorious and necessary truths are all the more confirmed thereby. Thus, this name would indicate the *unchangeability* of God’s Counsel (*Hebrews 6:17*), because a Testament is a Last Will, and as such is fixed and not changed. Thus, it must also follow that the Decree of Election concerns specific individuals, whose names are therefore said to be written in the *Book of Life*, as noted above; and who are therefore called <gloss>kekleemenoi</gloss> <note>original: κεκλημένοι; the "called" ones</note>, specifically in this Testament (*Hebrews 9:15*), with reference to a human testament, in which the heirs are usually expressed by name. Thus, lastly, by this name it would be indicated that the execution of the Purpose of Grace depends on the <term>Surety-death</term> <note>the death of Christ acting as a legal guarantor or "Surety"</note> of the Testament-maker (*Hebrews 9:15–18*); who in a special way is the Son, according to *Luke 22:29*: "I make to you by Testament the Kingdom."

One cannot deny that this view is presented and urged with an appearance of truth and utility; and one must not doubt that it is taught with a good intention by many prominent Theologians. However, it is also the case that no less famous and great men—

# P R E F A C E

...among us, who do not dare to give this name of TESTAMENT—neither as a *scriptural* name nor as a fully appropriate one—to the eternal decree of Election. This is not out of a desire to contradict everything or to find fault with even the best matters learned from others: But because, after a diligent and humble investigation, imitating the noble Bereans <note>A reference to the inhabitants of Beroea in Acts 17:11, who studied the Scriptures daily to see if what they were taught was true</note>, they have not been able to find sufficient grounds to do so. They know well that Holy Scripture speaks of an ETERNAL TESTAMENT; but they have also learned from the language of the Saints that *Eternal* is sometimes said of that which indeed had a beginning, but which is of a very long, constant, and even endless duration. In this sense, they read of *Eternal hills* in *Genesis 49:26* and *Deuteronomy 33:15*; of an *Eternal Covenant* between God and every living soul and all flesh that is on the earth in *Genesis 9:16*; and of an *eternal Gospel* in *Revelation 14:6*. Therefore, the word *eternal* here is not decisive proof for an eternity 
<margin>Cocceius, *On the Covenant*, Sections 246, 248, and *On Hebrews* 13, Section 76.</margin>
that is without beginning. Added to this is that some of those famous men who call Election an ETERNAL TESTAMENT, in the passage of Paul in *Hebrews 13:20*, explain the word *eternal* as a constant duration looking forward. They say that the *New Testament* is so named in contrast to the *Old* and *First* (*Hebrews 8:13*), which was near to vanishing, because this *New Testament* shall be constant until the end of the ages, is confirmed by the death of the *Testator* <note>The one who makes a will; in this context, Christ</note>, and because the goods promised therein will be enjoyed by the Heirs in eternity; following *Psalm 89:29, 34–36; Isaiah 54:10, 55:13; Jeremiah 33:20–21, 25–26;* and *Romans 11:29*.

Indeed, a certain learned and famous writer, who is otherwise not averse to calling the decree of election a *Testament*, says in his explanations of this passage: 
<margin>Johannes d'Outrein.</margin>
> Some prominent theologians think here of the general Testament of Grace, which would be called eternal because it extends through all three Economies <note>Theological periods: the Promise, the Law, and the Gospel</note>—under the Promise, the Law, and the Gospel. Yet we cannot give our consent to that... The Apostle understands here by the Eternal Testament the same thing by virtue of which the heirs receive the eternal inheritance. And that he explicitly calls the New Testament in *Hebrews 9:15*: And, just as he speaks here of the Blood of the Eternal Testament, so he had said there that his death had intervened for the redemption of transgressions and the obtaining of the Eternal Inheritance.

And as for the TESTAMENT that was PREVIOUSLY *confirmed by God in Christ*, as Paul writes in *Galatians 3:15–18*: *Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; though it be but a man's COVENANT* (<gloss>diatheke</gloss> <note>original: διαθήκη; a Greek term that can mean both a "covenant" or a "last will and testament"</note> TESTAMENT) *that is confirmed, no man annulleth, or addeth thereto. Now to Abraham and his seed were the PROMISES spoken. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ. And this I say: The COVENANT* (<gloss>diatheke</gloss> TESTAMENT) *that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the LAW, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the PROMISE of none effect. For if the INHERITANCE be of the LAW, it is no more of PROMISE: but God gave it to Abraham by PROMISE.* Thus it appears altogether very clear for—

<meta>This page continues the argument regarding the proper theological use of the word "Testament." <header>BY JOHANNES WESSELIUS</header>

...to arrive [at the point] that the Apostle certainly distinguishes the **LAW** from the *Epangelia* <note>original Greek: επαγγελια, meaning "Promise"</note> **PROMISE**, and from *Diathekee* <note>original Greek: διαθήκη, usually translated as "Covenant" or "Testament"</note> **TESTAMENT** or *Covenant*, and subordinates the Law to them; but that he takes **PROMISE** and **TESTAMENT** for one and the same thing, and uses them interchangeably as synonyms. For when he applies the analogy of a man’s *Diathekee* or **TESTAMENT** to Divine matters, he speaks first of the **PROMISES** spoken to Abraham and his offspring. To which *Promises* he subsequently gives the name of *Diathekee prokekyroomenee* <note>original Greek: διαθήκη προκεκυρωμένη, meaning "a covenant previously ratified"</note>, a previously confirmed *Covenant* or *Testament*, which is not made powerless by the **LAW**, so as to nullify it, that is, the **PROMISE**. And for this reason he also says afterward of the *Inheritance*, that it is not from the **LAW**, but from the **PROMISE**, because **PROMISE** and **TESTAMENT**, *Epangelia* and *Diathekee*, were the same. And this point is sufficiently agreed upon by that great Theologian <note>Johannes Cocceius (1603–1669), a famous Dutch-German theologian known for "Covenant Theology"</note>, who otherwise insists particularly on this passage for the name **TESTAMENT** to be given to the *Eternal Decree* <note>God's timeless decision regarding salvation</note>:

<margin>Cocceius, in *Theology*, Chapter XL, Section 18.</margin>
as he writes: *“The Apostle does not doubt in the least to call God's* **WILL**, **INDICATED** *through the Promise, a* **TESTAMENT**, *just as also the supreme* **PROMISE ITSELF**, *per metonymiam scilicet* <note>Latin: "by means of metonymy, naturally"—a figure of speech where a thing is called by the name of something closely associated with it</note>, *that is, to be known as an improper naming. In which manner (namely, improperly), we also tend to call the* **WORDS EXPLAINING** *the Last Will, or the* **INSTRUMENT** <note>In a legal sense, a formal document or deed</note>, *in which that same will is declared, a* **TESTAMENT**. *And the Latin word (Testamentum) signifies rather the* **WORDS** *of the one who appoints the heir: But the Greek* Diatithesthai <note>The verb form of "Diathekee," meaning "to dispose" or "to make a will"</note> *signifies first the act of the mind and will.”* In this way, he [Cocceius] indeed allows that the Apostle here gives the name of **TESTAMENT** not to the internal and Eternal **WILL** of God *alone*, but insofar as it is **INDICATED** by the Promise, and consequently to the **PROMISE** itself. But when he adds that this happens *improperly* <note>non-literally or figuratively</note>, he assumes that the word *Diathekee* properly signifies the internal decree of the Will to make someone an Heir, and improperly the outward Declaration of the same, by a manner of speaking where the name of the cause is used for the effect, or the preceding for the consequence. Which assumption by that Great Man will not be easily proven either from the origin of the word *Diathekee*, nor from its use by Sacred or Secular writers. And much less [can it be proven] that we tend to call the *words explaining the Last Will or the legal Document* a Testament **IN SUCH A MANNER**, *that is, also IMPROPERLY*. For it is indeed evident that we speak improperly when we give the name of someone's *Last Will* to their Testament; but that we speak very properly when we call the legal and formal Declaration of that Last Will a *Testament*. And the Learned Man appears to agree with this again, when he adds almost in the same breath that the Latin word *Testamentum* much rather signifies the *Outward Declaration* through words or writing than the internal Will. Therefore, it is judged not without reason that in this passage from the *Epistle to the Galatians*, **DIATHEKEE**, *Covenant* or *Testament*, or rather *Testamentary Covenant*, is the **PROMISE**, and specifically that which is found in *Genesis 22:18*: *“And in your seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed.”* In which words is the **TESTAMENT** of grace,

# PREFACE

or a solemn **DECLARATION** of God’s Eternal and unchangeable, and as it were **LAST WILL**, to send the Christ—that seed of Abraham par excellence—in the flesh, and to bless—that is, to justify and to save—all nations (that is, the elect out of all nations: first from the Israelites before the coming of that seed, and thereafter from the Gentiles after His coming) through faith *being in that seed* and united with the same. And this *Testament* was *confirmed* **BEFOREHAND**, prior to the *Law* of Moses, because it was a Divine and absolute Promise, which must surely be unchangeable; as also because the Lord’s Oath was added to it, *Gen. XXII. 16–18; Hebr. VI. 17, 18; Luke I. 72–75.* And furthermore, also because the elect, not only from Abraham’s house and lineage but also from other nations—*Canaanites* and *Arabs*, along with *Melchizedek, Job, Elihu*, and others—were justified and saved through faith alone in that *seed of the Woman* <note>A reference to the first prophecy of a savior in Genesis 3:15</note> for such a long time before the *Law*. For which reason also the Christ is possibly called the *Desire* **OF ALL NATIONS** <note>original Latin/Dutch: "Wensch aller Heidenen"</note> *Haggai II. 8*, because not only would all sorts of Gentiles desire Him after He was revealed in the flesh, but also because even before Moses’ *Law*, some chosen ones among the nations, like Job, had desired Him *Job XIX. 25, 26, 27.* And it is not improbable that Paul has this in mind when, looking at the preaching of the Christ among the Gentiles through the *Gospel*, he says that God **AGAIN** brought the *Firstborn* into the world *Hebr. I. 6*, because He had already allowed Him to be preached to the world once *before*, prior to the *Law* of Moses, through the Word of the Promise. Of this *Testament* of grace, Paul might also well say that it was previously confirmed by God Ἐις Χριστὸν <note>original Greek: eis Christon</note> **TO CHRIST**, to whom it was promised: *verse 19* <note>Galatians 3:19</note>, namely that the nations should recognize and glorify Him as the cause of their salvation through *faith*, love, and steadfast obedience. However, if one would rather translate these words *eis Christon* (as our version does) with **UPON CHRIST**, then the sense would be—if one joined them with the word *Diatheke* <term>Testament or Covenant</term>—that this referred to *Christ*, signified under the name of Abraham’s seed. And if one connected them with the word *confirmed*, it could mean that this *Testament* and *Covenant* were confirmed upon Christ's death as a surety <note>Though the death had not yet happened historically, it was the legal basis for the agreement</note>, which had not yet actually occurred but was prefigured and sealed before the *Law* in the sacrifices of the Patriarchs. Yet, if one would even rather translate *eis Christon* as **THROUGH CHRIST**, this could lead us to the account of Moses in *Gen. XXII. 11–18*, to think that the *Angel of the Lord*, who spoke those words—*In your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed*—was the *Christ Himself*, the Eternal Will of the Father (which was also the Son's will) revealing it there to Abraham; and thus rightly deserving the name of *Testament-maker* and Angel of the *Testament* <note>original: "Engel des Testaments," often translated as "Messenger of the Covenant"</note> *Hebr. IX. 16; Mal. III. 1*, even before His Incarnation. And finally, because in this **TESTAMENT** the blessing—that is, the **JUSTIFICATION** of the nations—was promised and granted solely through faith in this seed of Abraham, Paul might well call that grace of justification an **INHERITANCE**, which could be obtained *not from the Law*, or its works and own righteousness, but only from the faith of the *Promise*: just as elsewhere this benefit, which is irrevocable, is noted as the *Inheritance* of the believers *Isaiah LIV. 17; Hebr. IX. 15, XI. 7.*

# BY JOHANNES WESSELIUS.

<margin>Luke 22:29.</margin>
With no greater grounds is it judged that the passage *Luke 22:29* is brought forward: *And I <gloss>diatithemai</gloss> <note>original Greek: διατιθεμαι</note> appoint unto you a Kingdom, even as my Father <gloss>dietheto</gloss> <note>original Greek: διεθετο</note> has appointed unto me.* For the word *Diatithesthai*, from which *Diatheke* <note>The Greek word usually translated as "Covenant" or "Testament"</note> originates, and which is found here twice, signifies all kinds of appointments or arrangements: as much of ourselves—our minds and words—as over other matters. These occur: Either internally through our *Thoughts* and *Will*; (*He arranged the ascents in his heart <note>original Greek/Latin: "anabaseis en tee kardia hautou diétheto," Psalm 84:6</note>*) Or externally, through *Sale*, through *Promise*, (just as *to promise faithfulness <note>original Greek: "pistin diatithesthai," Nehemiah 9:38</note>*) and by *Command*, see *Joshua 7:11*, where *diatithesthai* is used for the Hebrew word <term>Tzivva <note>ציוה: To command or ordain</term></note>) and especially by way of *Covenant* negotiations, (*2 Chronicles 7:18. so will I establish the Throne of your Kingdom, even as I <gloss>diethemen</gloss> <note>original Greek: διεθεμην</note> have made a covenant with your Father David.*) And also in the manner of a *Testament* *Hebrews 9:17*, where *<gloss>diathemenos</gloss> <note>original Greek: διαθεμενος</note>* is a *Testator* <note>One who makes a will</note>.

But it is uncertain and cannot well be determined which of these meanings is the primary and proper one; whether that of an internal arrangement in our hidden will, or that which occurs externally at the same time by *Sale, Command, Promise, Covenant,* and *Testament*. Yet, if one wished to make some determination here, it would have more appearance of truth to say that this word *diatithesthai* held the meaning of external arrangement earlier than that of mere internal intent. But, because this internal arrangement by the will is always presupposed in the external *Covenant* and *Testament-making* (for irrational beasts make no Covenants or Testaments), this same word was therefore also taken for that internal arrangement of the Will. 

Be that as it may, it is nevertheless certain that these meanings are distinct, such that the meaning of internal arrangement of the Will can indeed take place alone, without the external declaration of the same through certain signs by way of *Covenant* or *Testament*, but the latter can never exist without the former. Therefore, one could indeed understand the internal arrangement of the Will here, without any external *Covenantal* or *Testamentary Declaration*, in this manner: I arrange, that is, I have arranged, in my eternal Divine Will, the Kingdom for You, just as my Father has appointed that for me in his Eternal decree. 

Yet, because it seems strange that our Savior, speaking of his eternal Will, uses the present tense, and of that of the Father, the past tense, whereas it is nevertheless one eternal, essential Divine will; it is therefore better to take this word *diatithesthai* here for the external declaration of that Eternal Divine Will: so that the sense of Christ’s words is this. I declare presently, according to my eternal purpose, as by a solemn *Covenant*, and as it were with a precious Oath, or otherwise as by *Last Will* and *Testament*, You by name, to be Heirs of the Kingdom, and I go now to seal this my *Covenant* with my own atoning blood, or to confirm my *Testament* with my death, not to vacate and empty the Inheritance for you (which happens through the death of mortal men), but to earn it for you through my Surety-death <note>The death of Christ acting as a legal guarantor or "Borg"</note>, I who am the God-man, and likewise for all my elect *Hebrews 9:15, 16, 17.* And that just as my Father, according to his Eternal Counsel, has declared to me with a precious Oath, to be found in the Tables of the Old Testament *2 Corinthians 3:14* by Moses and the Prophets, that

<meta>This page continues Wesselius’s linguistic exploration of the terms "Covenant" and "Testament." He is shifting focus from the specific actions of Christ to the broader theological implications of the "Eternal Decree of Election," arguing that while the Greek and Hebrew terms for "Covenant" are often translated as "Testament," the concept of a "Testament" (as a last will) technically refers to the public declaration of God's will rather than His hidden, eternal plan.</meta>

->PREFACE<-

through faith in me all the nations of the earth would be blessed and justified *Gen. 22:16, 18; Heb. 6:17* and that I would have the Heathen for my *Inheritance*, and the ends of the earth for my possession *Psalm 2:8.* indeed that I would be a Priest after the *Order of the account of Melchizedek <note>Melchizedek was a mysterious king and priest in the Old Testament whom Christians view as a "type" or foreshadowing of Christ</note>, that is, also at the same time King of peace and of righteousness*, unto eternity. *Psalm 110:4; Heb. 7:20, 21.* Surely in this manner the full meaning of the word *diatithesthai* <note>original Greek: διατίθεσθαι, meaning to arrange, appoint, or make a covenant</note> is satisfied, and at the same time the various expressions found here, when Christ speaks of his own deeds in the present, and of his Father’s deeds in time past.

From all of which it is again easy to gather that in this place the name of TESTAMENT or TESTAMENT-MAKING is not given separately to the *Eternal Decree of Election* <note>The theological concept of God's sovereign and eternal choice of those who will receive salvation</note>. It is also noteworthy that the Hebrew word *Berith* <note>original Hebrew: ברית, usually translated as Covenant</note> in the Old Testament is sometimes taken for an absolute Establishment of something, without any Condition added in the manner of a covenant; but in such a way that it nevertheless never signifies the hidden intention of God alone, but rather His solemn declaration, as can be seen among others in that cited passage from *Jeremiah 33:20, 21*, where the *Berith Covenant of the day and of the night* is spoken of; compared with *Genesis 8:22*, where we find this *Berith* or declaration of God's purpose thus: *Henceforth all the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.* This is also sufficiently admitted when one, looking at this passage of Jeremiah, says,
<margin>Johannes Cocceius, *Selected Disputations*, XIX. §. 7.</margin>
that the word *Berith* there signifies *the purpose explained in set words* <note>original Latin: "propositum conceptis verbis explicatum"</note>, that is, the *Purpose of God explained with clear words*.

We may therefore well conclude that this name of TESTAMENT, which is given to the Eternal Decree of Election, is not SCRIPTURAL; that is, it is not expressly found therein, neither under the Hebrew word *Berith*, nor under the Greek *diatheke* <note>original Greek: διαθήκη, meaning covenant or testament</note> and *diatithesthai*. And this Great Theologian <note>Johannes Cocceius (1603–1669), a highly influential Dutch-German theologian famous for "Federal Theology," which organized the Bible around a series of covenants (testaments)</note>, who otherwise insists so much on this matter, seems to acknowledge this sufficiently when He says in various places in his writings that the outward Declaration of God’s Eternal Will to save sinners through Christ is called a *Testament* in Holy Scripture.

### BY JOHANNES WESSELIUS.

<margin>
The Sum of the Covenant, Topic XVIII, Chapter 54, Section 3.
[Johannes] d'Outrein.

[These terms] are set down everywhere in the Scripture for the *Declaration* of God’s unchangeable Will. For among the Jews, the word *diatiki* <note>original Hebrew/Greek: דיתיקי / διαθήκη, usually translated as "testament" or "disposition"</note> signifies the word, the *command*, or the outward *disposition* and *arrangement* made by mouth or in writing, especially by one who is terminally ill, as His Honor <note>referring to a cited scholar, likely d’Outrein</note> himself testifies. This is also strongly confirmed in *The Covenant* through the learned notes of TREMELLIUS <note>Immanuel Tremellius was a 16th-century Jewish-Italian convert and leading Hebraist</note> on *Hebrews* 9:16, section 470. For which reason the previously cited learned writer, in his explanation of *Hebrews* 13:20, acknowledges that the general *Purpose* of grace is NEVER, in plain and direct words, called a TESTAMENT, looking specifically at the writings of the New Testament, as His Honor explains in the *Notes*. However, His Honor adds that it can indeed be called a Testament *according to Scripture, or by analogy of the Holy Scriptures*; just as one borrows words and expressions from Holy Scripture to teach and express one’s thoughts.

But if one teaches that the General Purpose of God’s Grace is never called a TESTAMENT, one must also admit that the *First* or *Old* and the *New Testament* are not directly the *Eternal Divine PURPOSE*, but rather its First or Old and New DECLARATION. The reason is that God’s *Purpose* is an *internal* and *abiding* act of the Divine Will, in which consequently no *Earlier* or *Later*, no *Old* and *New* can take place. But its *Declaration* is an external and transitory act—or rather, a product of that Eternal Divine Will—which therefore can be *Old* and *New*, *Earlier* and *Later*, and can be so named.

I would not, however, wish to argue over whether God’s Eternal Purpose of Grace might or could be called a TESTAMENT *figuratively*, either through *Agreement* with some similar-sounding expressions or by some *Conclusion* drawn from it; since my primary objective was to investigate whether this name was also *expressly* found in Holy Scripture as a substitute for the Eternal Decree. Meanwhile, one could very much doubt whether many such expressions actually occur in Holy Scripture. Eternal Election is indeed called a *Predestination for adoption as children* in *Ephesians* 1:5, and thus for *Heirs* in *Romans* 8:17; but that cannot make that Election—which is God’s internal and hidden Will—into a *Testament*, which is a *Declaration* of the Last Will. The pre-ordained Grace and Glory is often called an *Inheritance* in *Matthew* 25:34, *Colossians* 1:12, *Hebrews* 9:15, etc.; but it does not follow from this that the internal Pre-ordination itself is a *Testament*. Rather, it follows that the possession of the great pre-ordained good shall be permanent, and is most lawful, and flows from voluntary promises of grace found in the word of the Old and New Testaments, and is confirmed by the death of the *Guarantor* <note>Dutch: "Borge," a legal term for one who takes responsibility for another's debt; here referring to Christ</note> and *Angel of the Testament*, or the *Testament-maker*, in whom *all the promises of God are Yea and Amen* (2 Corinthians 1:20). And since Eternal Predestination is distinguished from the Calling in God’s word, I do not dare to claim that the word *called* in *Hebrews* 9:15 is a description of the *Elect*, as those named (nuncupati) <note>original Latin: "named" or "designated"</note> by the *Eternal Testament* in the decree of Election. Even if one conceded that those *Called* there, in that passage to the Hebrews, *were named by Testament*, one can surely think appropriately of the Testaments of Promise (*Ephesians* 2:12), in which the Elect from among the Gentiles were also specifically named, to become co-heirs of those eternal...

-> **PREFACE** <-

**Eternal Inheritance.** It is true that the **Eternal Decree of Election** <term>Eeuwig Besluit der Verkiefinge: The theological doctrine that God, from eternity, chose specific individuals for salvation.</term> is called, by way of metaphor, an enrolling of our names in the **Book of Life**: but it is by no means certain which human book or record is being alluded to in that figure of speech: Whether it is a **Family Register** <note>original: "Stamboek"</note>, in which the names of certain prominent men and good friends are recorded; or a **Military or Muster Roll**; or rather a **Citizenship Roll**, specifically that of the ancient earthly Jerusalem. This last view is judged by **Mr. PICTET** <note>Benedict Pictet (1655–1724), a prominent Swiss Reformed theologian often cited in Dutch academic works.</note>, in Book VIII, Chapter V, to be the most probable of all; he compares this not only to the customs of the Romans and other nations, but especially to those of the Jewish people in *Nehemiah 7:5, 12:23,* and *Ezekiel 13:9,* to which cited passages one may add *Isaiah 4:3.*

However, should anyone—believing that this figure of speech is taken from a **Testament** <note>In this context, a "Testament" refers to a legal "Last Will and Testament."</note>—wish to call God’s Eternal Foreknowledge and Purpose of grace by this name in a refined doctrinal sense, we do not believe that doing so would provide any great occasion for the harmful and absurd consequences that some attempt to draw from it with a great show of reasoning. For it is said that: if the Eternal Will of the Father to give the Kingdom to the Son were a *Testament*, then the Father would also have had to die to confirm His Will, based on the nature of the metaphor and the reasoning of Paul in *Hebrews 9:16, 17:* **A Testament is in force after men are dead** <note>original: "Een Testament is vast in de dooden"</note>, or **death**; indeed, it is argued that the Son would then be an **Heir** by virtue of a voluntary *Testament*, and not by **Nature**. Truly, such arguments have little foundation or appearance of valid logic. One must not apply metaphors borrowed from human affairs to Divine matters in every detail, nor too precisely. One satisfies this metaphor regarding the Father’s Eternal Will by saying that it is called a **Testament** to indicate its *immutability*: all the more so since the Father granted the Inheritance to the Son on the condition of the sacrifice of Himself in an assumed Humanity. For here, the death of the Testator was not required so that the inheritance could be granted to the Heir (as if vacated by its previous possessor), but rather so that the inheritance might be *earned*—which the Son alone was willing to do. And furthermore, it is also very certain that the Son has been established as a **Testament** <note>original: "Testamente"</note> from the beginning of the world, or declared **Heir** of all things, in order to govern them for the benefit of His **Elect**. But He could not have become such an Heir by Testament if He were not the **Heir by Nature** by virtue of His Eternal Sonship.

Cocceius and Aphorisms <note>original: "Aphoz," likely referring to Johannes Cocceius's "Aphorismi."</note>: a more detailed disputation 18, section 19, on Hebrews 7, section 103.
</margin>

It is currently the view of very orthodox theologians to posit an **ETERNAL COVENANT OF PEACE** between the Father and the Son. And a certain great and famous theologian <note>Likely referring to Johannes Cocceius (1603–1669), the father of "Covenant Theology" in the Netherlands.</note> has insisted upon this conception above others. He desires that the Eternal Decree of Election should have the form not only of a *Testament*, but also of a **COVENANT**, according to its various relations. Thus he says: *Insofar as the Father and the Son are distinct Persons, and are distinctly active in this Economy <note>The "Economy" here refers to the "Economy of Salvation," or the specific roles the Father, Son, and Spirit play in redeeming humanity.</note>, the single Will is called a* **COUNSEL OF PEACE** *between them both, as in Zechariah 6:13, and a* **COVENANT** or **TREATY**, *as in Isaiah 49:8.* And in another place—

<meta>The previous page discussed the "Covenant of Redemption" as a formal legal agreement between God the Father and God the Son. -># PREFACE<-
<meta>catchword: unity</meta>

...unity; whether it be by virtue of the cited passages of Holy Scripture. But also because very great difficulties appeared to me in this matter, which I have not yet been able to overcome.

I say that I find *no great necessity* in establishing such an *Eternal Covenant* between the Divine Persons, based on the nature of the matter itself. Because: once the eternal and independent Will of the triune God is established—to save some from fallen humanity through the intervening obedience and suffering of the Son as a <term>Surety</term><note>A "Surety" is a legal guarantor who takes responsibility for another's debt. In 18th-century theology, Jesus is described as the Surety who pays the "debt" of sin owed by humanity.</note>, to be undergone and fulfilled in a Human Nature to be assumed by Him in due time, according to the Lord’s Proprieties: from this it must follow that the salvation of those Elect who would live before the actual satisfaction of that future Surety would also be secured. Since the Eternal Divine Will was unchangeable, and that future Satisfaction of the Son was thereby fully certain and infallible. From which it follows that, to apply the pre-ordained salvation to those Elect before the actual payment by the Surety, it was not necessary that a Covenant be made between the Divine Persons, and established by the same, that the Redemption and salvation of some Elect should precede the paying of the Ransom. For this, the simple, eternal, and unchangeable Will of the triune God was sufficient. 

By virtue of which it also happened that immediately after the Fall, when Subjects of Divine grace were actually found, this *Eternal Purpose* of God was made known, the way of salvation revealed, the coming of the Divine Surety and Mediator promised, and prefigured through shadowy Offerings, Priests, and Sureties. It was foretold through Divine physical appearances and <term>manifestations</term><note>original: "speelingen." This refers to "Christophanies"—appearances of the Son of God in human or angelic form before his actual birth as Jesus.</note> in the world of the earth, *Proverbs 8:31*, and the forgiveness of sins and eternal life were promised, under the condition of faith in that future Surety. This faith was active through a Holy walk, and through Love of God and neighbor, according to the Royal Law, solemnly proclaimed on Sinai, with the addition of many other Laws as appendages, suited to the occasion of that time and State of the Church. This also included certain statutes taken from the Old <term>Covenant of Works</term><note>The "Covenant of Works" is the theological term for the agreement God made with Adam in Eden, based on perfect obedience.</note>, as cited by Paul in *Galatians 3:11-12*; yet in such a way that everything had to be subservient to the Word of the *Promise*. 

Since in this *Revelation and Declaration* of the Eternal Purpose of grace there were two types of *Promises*: first, the *Absolute*, without any added Condition, such as the coming and satisfaction of the Divine Surety for salvation, first for the Jews, and thereafter also for the Gentiles, and so for all the Elect and Believers, *Genesis 3:15, 22:18*; and others presented under the condition of *Faith* in the Surety, working through *Love*, as shown in *Acts 10:43, Genesis 15:1, 17:1, Isaiah 28:16, Habakkuk 2:4* etc. Thus this *Declaration* of God's *Eternal Purpose* took on the form, partly of a *Testament* <note>In this context, a "Testament" is like a Last Will and Testament—a one-sided promise that takes effect upon death.</note>, and partly of a *Covenant of Peace and Grace*, and is therefore called the *First* and *Old Testament* or *Covenant*; being truly the *Covenant of Grace*. 

However, it produced a *miscarriage* or rather *Illegitimate Children*, and gave birth unto bondage, *Galatians 4:24* and begat *Ishmaelites* <note>The "Ishmaelites" here are a metaphor for those who try to earn salvation through their own efforts or the Law, rather than receiving it through the promise (like Isaac).</note>, through a great misunderstanding by many in Israel, to whom God gave no eyes to see, nor hearts to understand the end of the *Law*, which was Christ, *Deuteronomy 29:4, Romans 10:4*; and who foolishly took up this Old Covenant of Grace, because of those *Legal Appendages and Statutes*, as if it were a Covenant of Works, in order through their own obedience...

### BY JOHANNES WESSELIUS. ###

...to be justified through the [perfect] fulfillment of that Law. And not only was this *Word*, *Covenant*, and *Testament* of the Promise an effect of that Eternal *Unchangeable Will* of the triune God, but the pre-ordained salvation was also effectively applied to the *Elect* of those times, by virtue of that unshakable Decree of God, now revealed through those Promises. They are that Eternal People whom He has established and powerfully called, *Isaiah 43:7.* To them was granted the *Spirit of faith*, *2 Corinthians 4:13*, through which they fervently desired and embraced the Angel of the Covenant, *Malachi 3:1*, along with Abraham, the *Father of all who believe*, *Romans 4:11; John 8:56* <note>The original text cites "Job. VIII. 56," which is a common early modern printing error or OCR misreading for John 8:56, where Jesus speaks of Abraham seeing His day.</note>, and through which they *were justified* and led into eternal glory, *Romans 3:25-26; Hebrews 2:10.* Furthermore, since this Covenant and Testament of the Promise, and this application of salvation to the eternal People of that time, was a work of this Eternal Will of the triune God—and specifically of the Son's Will to become human in due time and, in His humanity, to become a <term>Surety</term><note>A "Surety" (Borge) is a person who takes legal responsibility for the debt or obligations of another. In this theological context, Christ is seen as the one who pays the spiritual debt of humanity.</note>—He could then be called the Mediator: both of Announcement, *1 Peter 3:19*, and of Intercession, *Job 33:23-24; Zechariah 1:12*, and of effectual Application. At that time, He was not the mediator *of the One God* <note>original: "des Eenen Godts"</note>, since He had not yet become a man dependent on God, but was the *One God Himself*, *Galatians 3:19-20.* Moreover, because the sending of the Son in the flesh was certain and necessary by virtue of that irreproachable Decree, He is rightly called in the Old Testament—on account of His future mission and its preceding effects—the Angel of the Lord, of God's presence, and of the Covenant. Finally, because God’s eternal Son only became the *Mediator of merit and actual acquisition* of salvation when He became man; it is for this reason that the "Immanuel God-man" is called in the Holy Scriptures the Mediator *between God and men, 1 Timothy 2:5*, and that JESUS is emphatically said to have **BECOME SURETY**, *Hebrews 7:22*, and that He is the Mediator of the New and better *Testament or Covenant*, *Hebrews 8:6; 9:15; 12:24*. This is because that Better and New Dispensation and administration of the Covenant of Peace began with the shedding of His surety-blood, *Matthew 26:28; Hebrews 12:24*, and was founded therein; the old shadowy sureties, priests, and sacrificial blood were abolished; the word of the Promise, which was confirmed by shadowy sureties, was exchanged for the Gospel of Fulfillment; and the Gentiles were also called into the fellowship of Abraham’s seed.

I therefore consider it unnecessary to dispute here with many over the name of **SURETY** and the word **SURETYSHIP** <note>original: "Sponsio" — a Latin legal term for a formal promise or guarantee made to a third party</note>; namely, whether the **ETERNAL WILL** of the Son to satisfy the sins of the Elect in an assumed humanity must be called a **SURETY-PROMISE** or **SURETYSHIP**; and consequently, whether the Son has been a SURETY from eternity. This much is certain to me: that from eternity, in His eternal and Divine Spirit, *Hebrews 9:14*, He possessed the WILL to become, in time, a **PROMISING** and simultaneously **PAYING** Surety in His assumed human nature. I also believe that the actual Surety-promise in this Mystery of our Redemption can be understood as nothing other than a voluntary submission under the Will of the Sovereign Overlord and highest Judge, according to what is written in *Jeremiah 30:21*: "I will cause him to draw near," and *Hebrews 5:4*: "And no one takes this honor for himself..."

### BY JOHANNES WESSELIUS.

...the actual Will of the Son, which preceded the cause itself, which was the **Surety-blood** <note>original: "Borgbloet." Just as it is necessary to understand such an eternal Covenant between the Father and the Son—neither by the nature of the matter itself, nor because of the name of *Surety* given to the Son in *Scripture*—so it is by no means made necessary by those cited passages from the *Prophetic Writings*.

To better understand these, it is first necessary to note that those Revelations and Visions which the Prophets had of this, and which were recorded for our instruction and comfort, were Foresightings and Paintings. In these, they saw future things—often joined together with past things—as if present before their eyes; and in which the Persons appeared and spoke exactly as they would and must speak for the execution of God's eternal Counsel at the time of the Fulfillment of these Visions and Prophecies.

When David wrote the *Second Psalm*, he saw in such a Prophetic Foresight the Son of God, having now become man, placed as an object of the raging fury of Jews and Heathens, aiming to root out Him and His Church. He hears the *Christian Church* express its faith and confidence regarding the vanity of the counsels and the futile efforts of all her haters in *verses 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: Why do the Heathen rage?* etc. He hears God the *Father* speaking here to the heart of His oppressed People, calling Christ His *King*, *anointed by Him* <note>original: "gesalst." Wesselius explains this as being chosen and declared as King.</note>, *that is, chosen and declared as Zion’s King; verse 6: Yet have I set my King upon Zion,* etc.

Indeed, he hears the *Son himself*—now not only having become man but also glorified at the Father’s right hand—speaking thus to give courage to His distressed Zion and to warn all her and His enemies in *verses 7, 8, 9: I will declare the decree: The LORD hath said unto me; Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee. Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.* If one wishes to argue that the word TODAY refers to the time of the New Testament, these words cannot be understood as having been spoken in the eternal Decree in such a way that it would then take on the form of a *Covenant*. Rather, the meaning must be: I shall tell of the *immutability* of that *Decree*, and of that *Pre-ordination* of me as Zion’s king, as evidenced in its execution upon me; namely: just as the Father from eternity has anointed and chosen me as king, even of the Heathen, so He has also in fact inducted me into the actual possession of that kingdom, with full power and right to now also rule all the Elect from among Jews and Heathen in grace, and to punish the rebellious in implacable disfavor forever.

# FROM JOHANNES WESSELIUS.

...eternal Will of the Son, which already preceded the cause itself, namely the **Surety-blood** <note>original: "Borgbloet." In these, they saw future things (often joined together with past things) as if present before their eyes; and in these visions, the Persons appeared and spoke just as they would and must speak for the execution of God’s eternal Counsel at the time of the fulfillment of these visions and prophecies.

David, when he wrote the **Second Psalm**, saw in such a prophetic fore-vision the Son of God, having now become man, placed as an object of the raging fury of Jews and Gentiles, aimed at rooting out Him and His Church. He hears the Christian Church express her faith and confidence regarding the vanity of the counsels and the futile efforts of all her haters in verses 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5: *Why do the heathen rage?* etc. He then hears God the **Father** speak to the heart of His oppressed people, calling Christ His King, *anointed by Him—that is*, chosen and declared as Zion’s King in verse 6: *Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion,* etc.

Indeed, he hears the **Son himself**—not only having become man now, but also glorified at the Father’s right hand—speaking thus to give courage to His distressed Zion and to warn all her and His enemies in verses 7, 8, and 9: *I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee. Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.* If one wishes to argue that the word **TODAY** <note>original: "HEEDEN." Wesselius is debating whether "Today" refers to eternal generation or the historical moment of Christ's resurrection and installment as King.</note> refers to the time of the New Testament, then these words cannot be understood as being spoken in the eternal **Decree** in such a way that the decree would thereby have taken on the form of a **Covenant**. Rather, the meaning must be: I shall recount the **immutability** of that **Decree** and of that **Fore-ordination** of me as Zion’s king, as evidenced in its execution upon me. Namely: just as the Father from eternity has anointed and chosen me as king, even of the Gentiles, so He has also in deed installed me into the actual possession of that kingdom, with full power and right to now rule in grace over all the Elect from among Jews and Gentiles, and to punish the rebellious in implacable disfavor forever.

<meta>This page continues Wesselius’s argument that certain biblical passages often used to prove an "eternal" covenant between the Father and the Son actually refer to a covenant established or revealed in time, specifically regarding Christ’s role as the God-man and Surety.</meta>

# PREFACE

But it is by no means necessary to translate the little word <term>חק</term> <note>original Hebrew: *chōq*</note> *Chook* in this place as *Decree*, or to understand it as the *eternal Divine Decree*. The *Chaldean Translator* <note>Referring to the Targum, an ancient Aramaic translation and commentary on the Hebrew Bible.</note> translates it as <term>קימה</term> <note>original Aramaic: *qeyama*</note> *kejama*, meaning *Covenant*. In that case, the sense could be: *I will tell of the Covenant that was established in time between the Father and me, the God-man. In this covenant, the Father—first pointing out its foundation and my earned kingdom, namely my eternal Divinity and Sonship, which added an infinite value to the brief but very real Surety-suffering <note>original: "Borglyden." This refers to Christ’s suffering in his role as a legal guarantor who pays the debt of others.</note> of my humanity—said to me: "You are my Son, begotten of me in the eternal Today."* And furthermore, in that covenant, He promised me—after I should have offered my Soul as a guilt-offering—that upon my rightful *Claim*, He would give the Heathen as my inheritance, and would cause me to triumph over all my enemies. 

It is perhaps best and simplest to translate this word *Chook* as *Jerome* <note>St. Jerome, the 4th-century translator of the Latin Vulgate.</note> and others do, as *Command, Ordinance,* or *Law*. In that case, the sense would be: *I will tell of a law, so that it may be a law for all peoples to be received by them in faith and obedience; namely, that I am declared by Him to be His Eternal and natural Son, and that I have the right and power, as a Surety made perfect through suffering, to rule over the Heathen.* Or: *I will tell of the Command that I myself have received; to claim—by virtue of the infinite worth of my Surety-suffering (being that of God's own Eternal Son) and by virtue of the Covenant made between me, the God-man, and the Father—the Heathen as my inheritance; as well as to crush all those who set themselves against my kingdom and to make them suffer eternal destruction as punishment.* 

Whereupon, finally, God the Holy Spirit, who spoke through *David* in 2 Samuel 23:2, takes up the word; He exhorts the *Kings and Judges of the earth*, along with all their subjects, to conform themselves to this *Command*, and to this *Law and Ordinance*. Acting thus with understanding, they are to serve the LORD with fear and to kiss His Son in faith and submission, since *only those who trust in him would be truly blessed* (Psalm 2:10-12). From all of this, it appears that there is indeed grounds in these words to include a temporal *Covenant of Peace established between the Father and the Son (now being the God-man)*, but not an *eternal* one.

Not everyone proposes such an *Eternal Covenant of Peace* between these Divine Persons, but some also bring forward the words of *Psalm 16:2*, which they translate from the Hebrew as follows: *You have said to the LORD, You are the Lord, my goodness is not UPON YOU.* They believe that there, the Messiah, being in suffering, had prayed to the Lord in the *first verse*: *Preserve me, O God, for I trust in you*. This was for *Preservation*, both of his soul—to the end that it might remain faithful, holy, and obedient in the midst of all those pains, insults, temptations, and agonies of Hell—and of his body—to the end that it might be preserved, not from death, but from corruption in the grave (verse 10). Now, in this *second verse*, the Father answers this prayer of the Suffering and nearly expiring Surety, to give Him courage and to strengthen His faith until the end, in this manner: *You have said* (the Hebrew word <term>אמרת</term> <note>original: *amart*</note> is in the *feminine* gender, referring, if one wishes, to his great physical weakening on the Cross, or rather to his human soul) *to the LORD, that is to me: You are the Lord; my good-* <meta>Catchword: goet- (good-)</meta>

# FROM JOHANNES WESSELIUS.

goodness—that is, grace, benefits, and gifts—is not UPON YOU; namely, to earn them. You have now satisfied my Demand; I require nothing more from You. Thus one finds here the *Eternal Covenant of Suretyship* <note>Dutch: *Eeuwig Borg Verbont*. A theological concept where Christ acts as a 'surety' or legal guarantor for humanity's debt to God.</note>, in which the Father had placed His goodness and grace, to be granted to the Elect, UPON the SON, so that He might acquire them through a weighty suffering as Surety; and simultaneously one in which—though later also in the actual execution—the *Son* had subjected himself to the Father’s will and command, and said, *you are the Lord, and I am your Servant*. Which *obedience* of the Son, both from *eternity* in the Covenant of Peace and demonstrated in time, the Father would then here approve, and accept as satisfying His justice and will.

It is well known how earnestly some Renowned Men, who are otherwise in favor of the *Eternal Covenant* between the Father and the Son, have for a long time declared themselves against this interpretation in their writings. And certainly, it is judged not without reason that the Messiah speaks in this entire *Psalm*. In the *First Verse* to his *Father*, and in the *Second* to his *human soul*; just as our Dutch translation has it: *O my soul, you have said to the* LORD, *You are the Lord: my goodness reaches not to you.* <note>A reference to Psalm 16:2. The author is debating whether the "goodness" refers to God's gifts to Christ, or Christ's merits which cannot "add" anything to God's perfection.</note> My Goodness—that is, innate Holiness and actual obedience unto the death of the Cross—reaches *not to You*, specifically so that Your infinite Greatness, All-sufficiency, and Blessedness could be increased in itself thereby; *but to the Saints who are on earth, etc.* In addition, it is noted that in the *second Verse* there can be no *Answer* or *Address* from the Father to the Son, because a *different person*, or *something else*, is addressed in the *feminine* <note>Referring to the Hebrew grammar of the original text, where the verb "you have said" is feminine, implying the speaker is addressing his "soul" (a feminine noun).</note>, *you [feminine] have said*, and another in the *masculine*, *my goodness is not to* or *upon You [masculine]*. It is also thought that if these were words from the Father to Christ, He would have spoken more clearly, having said, *you have said TO ME*, rather than, *you have said to the* LORD. It is further said that in these words of the Father to the Son, *You have said to the* LORD; *you are the Lord*, if they contained an approval of his suffering as Surety and his obedience, then a very faint depiction of that most wonderful and perfect obedience of God’s Eternal Son—humbled even to the death of the Cross, yes, even unto Hell—would be found. They add to this, moreover, that those words, *my goodness is not upon You*; if there were therein a *Declaration* of debt paid and of complete satisfaction to Divine Justice, then they would have no small amount of obscurity in them. At the very least, this could then be expressed much more clearly in this manner: *My Wrath, or my Law, or the Surety-suffering, Surety-obedience*, is not upon You. *You are henceforth not obligated to bear, or to obey, or to fulfill them.* For indeed, the Surety did not properly owe grace and goodness, but suffering and obedience, in order to acquire that *goodness of God* thereby. And finally, since the suffering Messiah remained indebted as long as the last farthing <note>original: *quadrant-penning*. A reference to the "uttermost farthing" in Matthew 5:26, symbolizing the total payment of a debt.</note> was not paid in His death; so, it is said, it could not be said so absolutely to Him, not yet having undergone all Satisfying suffering, MY GOODNESS IS NOT UPON YOU: but rather; either my goodness SHALL NOT *be upon You*, after the now-approaching ultimate step of Humiliation in death; or *rather* IS NO LONGER *upon You*, now agonizing on the Cross—that is then, *shall in a short time no longer be upon You*: just as the crucified Savior said in that sense before his death, *It is finished. John XIX. 30.*

a cause of His Incarnation, as some would have it, but as a consequence of the same, and most closely tied to it. Just as this is indeed very clearly explained in Chapter XLIX. 1. 3. 5. *Listen to me, you islands, and pay attention, you Peoples from afar, the LORD has CALLED me FROM THE WOMB, FROM MY MOTHER’S INWARDS he has MENTIONED MY NAME . . .* *And he said to me,* YOU ARE MY SERVANT . . . *And now says the LORD who FORMED me FROM (THE MOTHER’S) WOMB TO BE A SERVANT.* Furthermore, I read indeed that the LORD SAYS, *I will give you for a Covenant of the People,* as an Angel <note>Messenger</note>, Envoy, Announcer, Confirmer, and Executor of the Covenant established with the Chosen People. Yet not that the Lord said this to the Son of Eternity, but in the *Time of Favor*, and in the *day of Salvation* Chapter XLIX. 8. Further I observe: that, while such a glorious and Divine Office and Work is attributed here to this Servant of the Lord; so that no one might think, with the modern Socinians <note>A group that denied the full divinity of Christ, viewing Him as a man who became God-like</note>, that He was a Deified Human or a created God; not without great emphasis, in that same Discourse of the Father, the following is added, Chapter XLII. 8. *I am the LORD, that is my name: and my glory I will not give to another,* so as to indicate that this Servant of the Lord was at the same time the true and Highest God—distinct in person, but not in Divine Essence, another from the Father. And consequently, I find indeed ground to posit a *Covenant* made between the Father and the Son, now having come into the Flesh; by virtue of which He is called the Servant of the Lord, and the Father calls *Him His God*, and mentions a reward, when He says Chapter XLIX. 4. *Surely my right is with the LORD, and my reward is with my God:* But by no means to posit that this *Covenant* had actually taken place in such a way from eternity; although it was decreed from eternity by the Triune God.

Exactly the same must be said of that illustrious Prophecy, which is praised above others in this matter, and which is also found in Isaiah, Chapter LIII. 10. 11. *When his soul shall have made (itself) a guilt offering* (or as others read *When his soul shall have made a guilt offering,* or, *When You, O Lord, shall have made his soul a guilt offering,*) *so shall he see seed, he shall prolong the days:* (or, *that shall prolong the days*) *and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper through his hand. Because of the labor of his soul he shall see it, and be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my Servant, the righteous one, make many righteous, for he shall bear their iniquities.*

For here we find such words, which must necessarily have appeared to the Christ, now having come, and knowing that this was written of Him; as an Invitation, and as a Demand from the Father to Him to present Himself as a guilt offering, with an added Promise of and

<meta>This page continues the theological argument regarding Zechariah 6:12-13, specifically debating whether the "Counsel of Peace" refers to an eternal decree or a covenant established in time between the Father and the incarnate Son.</meta>

# FROM JOHANNES WESSELIUS

Now allow also that the word *Counsel* here does not signify a Deliberation, or a *Wise* Resolution and firm determination of the Will—as the Hebrew word *etsah* <note>original: עֵצָה, meaning counsel or advice</note> is very often taken—nor a mere *Agreement* and *Concurrence* of Wills, Efforts, and Purposes. Rather, it signifies a solemn *Obligation of Will*, or *Covenant*, which, because it is made among men following prior deliberations and resolutions, is therefore called a *Counsel* here by a figurative way of speaking. And consequently, I will also gladly allow that this *Counsel* or *Covenant* OF PEACE is a Covenant between the Father and the Son, to establish Peace between the Wrathful Judge of Heaven and Earth and the Chosen Sinner through the Suretyship and Atoning Blood of Immanuel.

From all this, if we wish to keep to the *letter* of the Text—from which one must never depart without sufficient reason—it must necessarily follow that such a *Covenant of Peace* between these two Divine Persons *was yet to be established*. For so the words sound: *And the Counsel of Peace SHALL BE between them both.* And who are those BOTH? The Father and the Son, before His Incarnation? No: but the Father and the Son, now also being a MAN, and a BRANCH and FRUIT OF THE EARTH, become so without the intervention of a man, through His own Divine Omnipotence from a Virgin, and so *branched out from under Himself (verse 12)*.

If it is said that it is not necessary to understand the word *tihyeh* <note>original: תִּהְיֶה</note>, SHALL BE, as referring to the *matter itself*, but that it can be understood as the REVELATION OF THE MATTER; in this manner: *And it shall be made manifest that there is a Counsel of Peace between those two, and has been from eternity*: then I answer that it is indeed true that in Holy Scripture certain things are sometimes said to have happened or that they shall happen, when the focus is merely on the *Revelation* of those things. If one wished to apply this figurative way of speaking here, then one would much better understand the *Internal Decree* of the Triune God, and particularly of the Father and of the Son, which would be *revealed* in the fullness of time, as having been taken from Eternity, *John 15:16; Acts 2:23, 4:27-28; 1 Cor. 2:7; 1 Pet. 1:19-20.* But if one maintains that this *Counsel of Peace* is an *Eternal Covenantal negotiation* between two Divine Persons; then one must again prove from elsewhere in Holy Scripture that such an *Eternal Covenant* was truly established: which has not happened until now. And therefore, there is not the slightest necessity here to employ such a figurative way of speaking. Also, this is truly very inappropriate in this place, in which the future tense is used more than once for the *Matter itself*, and not for its *Revelation*. Thus it is written of the *Man whose name is the Branch*, that He *SHALL branch out from His place*, and He *SHALL build the temple of the Lord*: *Yes, He SHALL build the temple of the Lord*, and He *SHALL bear the glory*, and He *SHALL sit and rule upon His throne*. Just as all this is understood of the Matter itself as being in the future, so also in that same way must that which follows be understood as being said of the Matter itself: and the *Counsel of Peace SHALL BE between them both*.

But besides all this, I am of the opinion, subject to correction, that the *Nature* of the matter of a true and substantial COVENANT between the Father and the

# PREFACE

### OF THE

# AUTHOR.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'D' containing an illustration of a man sitting in a landscape under a tree, possibly representing a scholar or biblical figure.</image-desc>

<margin>
On the
excel-
lence
and use-
fulness of
The-
ology.
</margin>
**T**heology <note>original: "God-Geleertheid," literally God-learning or Divinity</note> is beyond contradiction the most beautiful, the most sublime, and the most useful of all sciences. One will not doubt this if one pays attention to what it contains. It teaches us to know the first and most perfect of all beings, whom we call *God*, and describes all His perfections. It says that He is a pure and single Spirit, who is present everywhere, in Heaven, on the Earth, in the Abysses; who knows everything, not only the present and the past, but also the future. It gives us an idea of His infinite power, which founded the earth, expanded the heavens, and created the Universe out of nothing; of His incomprehensible wisdom, which governs and rules the world; of His unspeakable *mercy*, which shows grace to the repentant sinner; of His *justice*, which cannot leave sin unpunished; of the *State of Happiness* <note>original: "Gelukstaat," referring to the divine state of blessedness or beatitude</note> which He possesses, and which can be disturbed by no one; of His *Majesty*, which makes the Angels themselves stare in awe; of His faithfulness, eternity, glory; of the covenant that He has made with men; of the laws He has given them, and of the rewards or punishments He preserves for them.

It teaches man to know himself; it makes him know his nothingness before God, and the infinite distance that exists between him and the Creator. It depicts for him the glorious state in which God had placed him in the beginning. It describes, moreover, his lamentable fall, the ground of his misery, corruption, and weakness. It shows him the contaminated fountain-head of his evil desires before his eyes. It shows him his inability to escape from the abyss into which he has been plunged by sin, the guilt he has brought upon his neck by his crimes, and the necessity of God's grace. It convinces him of the shortness and fragility of his life, and gives him a vision of the immortality of his soul.

It discovers to him what God has done to make us Blessed <note>original: "Zalig," meaning saved or spiritually blissful</note>. It shows him the Son of God, who descends from the high heaven, becomes man by assuming human nature with its sinless weaknesses, dies a shameful death to satisfy for our sins, descends into a dismal grave, from which He rises gloriously and ascends to heaven, from where He sends out His servants to proclaim His Gospel, and pours out His Spirit upon men to enlighten them in their darkness, to deliver them from their corruption, to conquer their passions, to sanctify them, and to bring forth all Christian virtues in them.

Finally, it teaches them all they must do to please God, and what they have to expect after their death; the Salvation <note>original: "Zaligheid"</note> that is pre-
